@galicia-toolkit-nestjs-20-lite/archetype is a dependency confusion package published to npm on 2026-10-09 by the account s4yhii__, targeting the internal @galicia-toolkit-* / @brick-v2 package namespaces with inflated versions (e.g. 999.0.x). Early versions resolve <hostname>.<tag>.dc.oob.s4yhii.com via DNS to beacon the victim's hostname. Later versions run `node index.js` from a preinstall hook, which loads a bundled native addon (prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node, Linux and Windows builds). The addon forks a detached process that collects hostname, username, OS/arch, cwd and the full values of CI/cloud secrets from environment variables (NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN, AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT and others) and sends them as JSON via HTTP POST /native to oob.s4yhii.com:9999.

## Source: amazon-inspector (524c80bfea6a1b22cb0a4784d2763ccf83099faab3816c9fcb1ce39bb8813152)
On `npm install`, this package runs `node index.js || true` as a `preinstall` script. `index.js` loads a platform-specific native addon from `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node`. The Linux and Windows binaries contain the hardcoded host `oob.s4yhii.com` and a `POST /native HTTP/1.0` request line with a JSON template carrying `src`, `pkg`, `h` (hostname), `u` (username), `os`, `arch`, `rel`, `cwd`, and `e` (an environment-variable dictionary). The native code reads a hardcoded set of credential-bearing environment variables including AWS access keys, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, Azure DevOps PAT, and GitHub Actions runtime/ID tokens, and ships them to that host over a raw socket (getaddrinfo/connect/send; WS2_32 on Windows). The Linux variant uses fork+setsid to detach the exfiltration process from the install. The shipped JavaScript is a stub exporting empty `forRoot`/`createLogger`, with no real functionality beyond loading the addon. The package name uses a scoped namespace that resembles an internal toolkit and is published at version 999.0.3, a version-overshoot pattern consistent with dependency-confusion targeting private registries.
